title: Switchboard — oncall dossier (shift sketch)
content:
Purpose: scratchpad + short-lived procedures for the swing shift. Use this as the quick reference to get into the state, list of known issues, and what to leave for the next person. NOT authoritative — see Confluence runbook for full procedures (linked above).

Shift summary (what I saw at start):
- Cluster health: primary serving cluster (serving-prod-us-west) green from probe but degraded p95 for short sequences.
- Recent deploy: infra/k8s autoscaler change rolled around 02:10 UTC (PR #317) — watch pod churn patterns.
- Active tickets: INF-4820 (KV cache thrash, customer-facing latency), and INF-4817 (embed-worker OOM spikes).

Quick start checklist (first 15 minutes):
1) Pager and Slack: confirm I have page channel and PD escalation enabled (pd-schedule: "sre-oncall-west").
2) Check main dashboards: Console -> Per-route latency (last 1h) -> filter model: 'redwood/llama2-13b'.
3) Look at recent deploys: gh actions / GitHub -> last deploy time in infra namespace.
4) Query pods: kubectl -n serving get pods -o wide | grep CrashLoop
5) Check autoscaler events: kubectl -n infra get hpa -o yaml | grep -A3 "events"

Known issues (live):
- INF-4820: KV cache misses spike when sequence length sudden jump -> symptomatic of recent autoscaler plugin change. Customer reports intermittent 300–600ms added latency for prompt prefix reuse paths. Mitigation in place: manual cache-warm job (see below).
- INF-4817: embed-worker OOMs on large-batch jobs. Root cause suspected: batch-size heuristic not honoring per-tenant memory limits after worker restart. Currently mitigated by temporarily dropping max_batch to 8 for embed-workers (k8s config patch applied).

Temporary mitigations and commands (copy/paste friendly):
- Warm cache job (quick):
  kubectl -n serving run cache-warmer --image=redwood/cache-warm:latest --restart=OnFailure -- env-vars KEYSET=frequent-prefixes SCHEDULE=once
  (This triggers a one-off job that does prefix traversals to prime the in-memory KV caches; monitor memory usage - it spikes for ~2–3m)

- Reduce embed-worker batch size (applied by me at 03:05 UTC):
  kubectl -n serving set env deployment/embed-worker MAX_BATCH=8 --record
  watch kubectl -n serving get pods -l app=embed-worker -o jsonpath='{.items[*].status.containerStatuses[*].restartCount}'

- Roll back autoscaler plugin (if regressions escalate):
  1) kubectl -n infra set image deployment/autoscaler infra/autoscaler:stable-2026-02-17
  2) kubectl -n infra rollout status deployment/autoscaler
  Note: rollback will reduce the new adaptive frequency but avoid KV thrash; coordinate with release-eng on Slack (#release-coord).

Escalation contacts (order):
- Primary: Evan Brooks (SRE lead) — pager: +1-415-555-0146, slack: @evan (if not responding after 10m).
- Secondary: Sofia Alvarez (infra eng) — pager: +1-415-555-0222, slack: @sofia.
- If customer impact > 10% error or > 1s median latency across traffic: escalate to oncall-eng@redwood.com and page DRI on call.

Investigation notes (things to follow up):
- KV cache profile dump: I captured dumps at 03:18 UTC (s3://redwood-ops/dumps/kv-2026-03-12-0318.log). Need to parse for top-100 prefixes and add to cache-warm job input.
- Telemetry gap: traces for model route 'redwood/llama2-13b' show missing sampling for some spans (likely transient due to agent restart). Open an infra ticket to increase temporary sample rate for next 2h if we continue to see noise.
- Batch heuristic fix: PR in progress by infra team, review PR #322 and test on staging before promoting.

What to leave for next shift (concrete):
- Confirm INF-4820 latency decreased after two warm runs; if not, consider rolling autoscaler plugin back (steps above) and notify product-owner @maria.
- Watch embed-worker restart counts for 1h. If restarts > 3 within 30m -> revert MAX_BATCH change and escalate to Sofia.
- Add top-50 prefixes from KV dump to the warm list and run job during low-traffic window (04:30–05:00 UTC).

Parking lot / followups (non-urgent):
- Make cache-warm job paramizable and add to k8s CronJob with feature flag.
- Add metric alert for "kv_cache_miss_rate" > 0.02 for 5m for any route.
- Write a short playbook for cache warmers with runbook snippets and attach to Confluence.

Random notes / hacks used during shift: 
- When pods fail with ImagePullBackOff, sometimes the node has stale docker-layer cache. Draining the node and letting kube-scheduler place fresh pods can help fast (temporary).
- For a quick sanity check of latency source: curl the model endpoint from jump box with headers: X-Redwood-Debug:1 and compare server-timers header.

Post-shift handover message (to paste in Slack at end):
"Leaving at 07:00 UTC — primary cluster green but still watching INF-4820 (kv cache misses). Ran two cache-warm jobs; reduced embed-worker batch to 8; left notes for next oncall. Please escalate to Evan if p95 latency increases by >200ms from baseline. — Maya"

TODOS (for me / next shift):
- [ ] Parse kv dump and create warm-list (assign: Maya).
- [ ] Draft temporary alert for kv_cache_miss_rate (assign: next oncall or SRE infra).
- [ ] Follow up on PR #322 (batch heuristic).

Last thought: This doc is intentionally lightweight — treat it like a lab notebook. If you inherit a noisy cluster, prioritize customer-facing latency regressions over internal infra churn unless it's cascading.
